Priya to schedule a 90-minute benchmark with customer data slice
Customer to share sample inference payloads and peak qps by 2026-11-10
action_items: Alex Monroe | Grant 30k free credits & send pricing tiers | 2026-11-09
Priya Desai | Configure benchmark harness, add Redwood Dedicated config, invite Marcus | 2026-11-12

meeting_header:
Date: 2026-11-07 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Ethan Liu (Redwood Solutions), Nina Patel (Cobalt Orchard CTO), Marcus Hale (Infra), Sofia Rey (Product), Ben Ortiz (ML)
meeting_summary: Intro discovery for quicklaunch path: customer wants to validate Redwood hosted first, evaluate Dedicated/private for data residency later. Main asks: time-to-first-token (TTFT) using free credits, expected QPS & latency SLO, SOC2/KMS/SAML questions, and a benchmark run. Next steps: Redwood to provide credits + pricing, run benchmark, share security pack.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Monroe: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Priya and Ethan are with me from the solutions team. Could you do quick intros?
[00:17] Nina Patel: Sure, I'm Nina, CTO at Cobalt Orchard, we run a B2B forms-extraction product, so inference for document parsing is our main path. Marcus is our infra lead, Sofia is product, Ben is ML.
[00:35] Priya Desai: Nice to meet you all. Quick note, today's goal is to understand your success criteria for TTFT -- time-to-first-token -- and whether hosted vs dedicated vs private is the right path for the next sprint.
[00:50] Marcus Hale: Our main constraints: data residency for certain customers, plus predictable latency under 200ms 95th at our typical 6–8 rps baseline. Cost is important but not the only factor.
[01:09] Ben Ortiz: We typically run a batch of documents but have peaks; during parsing-heavy hours we can spike to ~60 rps for short periods.
[01:27] Alex Monroe: That's helpful. For a quicklaunch we usually recommend starting hosted so you can get TTFT fast — free credits, API keys, and usage dashboards — then if you need isolation we can move to Dedicated or Private.
[01:44] Sofia Rey: How fast is fast? Like, from signup to a token?
[01:52] Alex Monroe: We've seen teams go from sign-up to first request in under 30 minutes for basic flows; realistic end-to-end TTFT including getting sample payloads and running a small eval is 1–2 days. If you want a benchmark with your data and traffic profile, that can take a week to schedule and run.
[02:10] Marcus Hale: When you say Dedicated, that's reserved GPU capacity with an SLA right? What's the difference versus private?
[02:23] Priya Desai: Yes, Dedicated is a Redwood-managed pool — reserved capacity, predictable throughput and SLAs. Private adds your VPC/on-prem networking and often an air-gapped option plus KMS integration. We call out the differences in the doc I'll send.
[02:43] Nina Patel: Security questions: we need SOC 2, SSO via SAML/okta, audit logs, and KMS-based encryption.
[02:52] Ethan Liu: We support SOC 2, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and can integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments. On hosted, we offer encryption at rest and in transit; we also provide detailed access logs and token-level analytics.
[03:12] Ben Ortiz: And data retention? If we send customer PII through the API, can you guarantee deletion?
[03:18] Alex Monroe: We have configurable retention policies; for enterprise we support zero-retention or customer-managed retention for Private. We'll include the security pack with exact retention options.
[03:30] Sofia Rey: Pricing — how do credits map to tokens, and what's an expected cost per inference?
[03:38] Alex Monroe: We'll send a pricing sheet but rough mapping: credits are a pre-provisioned dollar-equivalent. Hosted per-token pricing varies by model, but typical open-models are lower cost than proprietary stacks. Also our Optimize product suggests batching and quantization to reduce unit cost.
[03:58] Marcus Hale: We're sensitive to latency-cost tradeoffs. If we quantize aggressively to save cost, can we expect regressions in parse quality?
[04:08] Priya Desai: There's a tradeoff, yes. For document parsing often we can use 8-bit quantized variants without meaningful quality loss, but we recommend running a small eval set — we'll do that in the benchmark.
[04:24] Nina Patel: On the pilot — what does Redwood need from us to get the TTFT under a day?
[04:30] Alex Monroe: Minimal: sign-up, one API key, a couple sample payloads, expected SLOs, and someone to run a quick smoke test. We'll provision credits immediately. For a full benchmark: sample dataset, expected traffic profile, and some success metrics.
[04:48] Ben Ortiz: Is there any special setup for our internal compliance process? We have some customers in EU so data residency matters.
[04:56] Ethan Liu: We can recommend region routing; hosted supports select regions and we can route EU requests to EU regions. For stricter residency or certification needs we usually recommend Private deployment in the EU region or an on-prem option.
[05:14] Sofia Rey: Competitors question — have you done similar migrations from Anthropic or OpenAI for customers?
[05:21] Alex Monroe: Yep, we've onboarded teams migrating from OpenAI and Anthropic; we have migration guides and often run A/B regressions to ensure parity. Sometimes customers keep a fallback to their previous provider for edge cases.
[05:36] Marcus Hale: For the benchmark, can we run it against both hosted and a Dedicated config to compare latency and cost?
[05:43] Priya Desai: Absolutely. We can run parallel tests: same model/quantization on hosted vs Dedicated nodes and show delta on p95 and cost per token. That helps inform a reserved capacity decision.
[06:00] Nina Patel: How long to spin up Dedicated capacity for a pilot?
[06:06] Priya Desai: For short pilots we have a 'burst' pool that can be used without a long-term commit; to get a reserved Dedicated set up with SLA it can be a couple of weeks depending on region.
[06:19] Ben Ortiz: Any friction points around VPC peering or private link?
[06:24] Ethan Liu: For Private we do VPC peering and provide an installer for on-prem; timing varies — peering is quick but the on-prem installer and KMS integration need coordination.
[06:34] Sofia Rey: Do you support function-calling / structured outputs for parsing?
[06:39] Priya Desai: Yes, Redwood supports structured outputs and function/tool calling; we also have guidance for making your prompts deterministic for parsing pipelines.
[06:52] Marcus Hale: Can we try a smoke test now? I have a small sample ready.
[06:57] Alex Monroe: We can do a live smoke if you're comfortable. Marcus, do you want to paste a sample or should we do it after?
[07:05] Marcus Hale: I'll paste a small doc — give me a second.
[07:15] [Crosstalk, typing sounds]
[07:30] Marcus Hale: Okay pasted.
[07:33] Ben Ortiz: Sorry, the sample is a 2-page lease agreement — nothing PII.
[07:37] Priya Desai: Great, we'll run a quick call: I'll show a curl example, but note transcript might mis-quote the curl.
[07:45] Priya Desai: (shares) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"input": "<doc>", "task": "extract"}'
[07:58] [00:07:58] Alex Monroe: The customer's pasted doc appears to have parsed fine in the smoke; I'm seeing expected fields. Marcus, did that match what you expect?
[08:06] Marcus Hale: Looks promising, latency around 180ms on that small test which is within our SLO.
[08:12] Alex Monroe: Great. We'll capture the exact headers and curl in the follow-up note.
[08:20] Nina Patel: For the benchmark data, what's the format you prefer? JSONL?
[08:25] Priya Desai: JSONL with labels for expected extraction is ideal. If it's large you can share a sample subset first.
[08:33] Ben Ortiz: About trust and egress, if we do Private will logs ever leave our VPC?
[08:37] Ethan Liu: In Private deployments logs stay in your environment; in Dedicated there's a managed plane but you can enable strict audit logging and export to your SIEM.
[08:49] Sofia Rey: Can you also show us a quick dashboard — per-route latency and token cost?
[08:54] Alex Monroe: We'll include screenshots in the follow-up; our Console shows per-route breakdowns and token-level cost.
[09:02] Nina Patel: Decision timeline: we aim to pick a path by end of November. We want a pilot running in first half of December if possible.
[09:12] Alex Monroe: That aligns well. I'll get the credits provisioned today and send the security pack + pricing. Priya will own the benchmark scheduling.
[09:22] Marcus Hale: Any blockers on our side beyond sharing samples and a test account?
[09:27] Alex Monroe: No blockers. For Private we might need legal to review the installer terms but that's later.
[09:34] Sofia Rey: Quick ask — can you include an example of quantization impact on parsing accuracy in the docs?
[09:41] Priya Desai: Yes, we'll include a short eval showing 8-bit vs 16-bit quality on a small annotation set.
[09:49] Nina Patel: Thanks, this was helpful.
[09:52] Alex Monroe: Cool. To recap: we'll grant 30k credits, send pricing/security docs, and schedule a benchmark. Next meeting to be post-benchmark to review results.
[10:05] Nina Patel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:09] [Meeting ends]
